scope: additive stable anchor and rare-site booster selected from the frozen invariant nonlinear audit on folds 3 and 4

anchor.selection_evidence: at strength 0.20, whole AP +0.003258 with paired-site lower bound +0.000010 and positive fold/sensor deltas

booster.selection_evidence: at strength 0.10, low-prevalence AP +0.018270 with positive fold/sensor deltas; its only point failure was whole fold 3

component_contract.base_normalization: unlabeled rank/inverse-normal within each fold x sensor
component_contract.orientation: direction learned only from the opposite fold
component_contract.post_transform_normalization: unlabeled mean-zero/unit-variance within each fold x sensor
component_contract.composition: exact current-score logit plus anchor_strength*anchor plus booster_strength*booster

target_domain.name: low-prevalence physical-location proxy for the official test-only-site view
target_domain.membership: all rows from physical_location_id groups whose combined folds-3/4 positive rate is <=0.05
target_domain.use: evaluation and gating only; no site prevalence or labels enter either component

invariants: Both component features independently passed the original invariant univariate evidence gates.
The anchor transform is the only nonlinear candidate with a strictly positive whole-view paired-site AP lower bound.
The booster transform produced the largest stable low-prevalence point gain among the nonlinear candidates.
Every represented sample comes from an adapter that excluded its fold.
Feature directions are learned only from the opposite fold.
All normalization and gating operations are label-free.
The low-prevalence definition affects evaluation only.
Both whole-development and low-prevalence paired-site AP lower bounds must be strictly positive.
A development pass can only authorize a separately frozen fold-2 confirmation.
Fold 2, fresh data, and exact-paper inputs are never loaded.
